MIT.overview: Massachusetts Institute of Technology — world leader in science, engineering, and technology. Extremely competitive with ~3.9% acceptance rate.
what_matters: Unique spikes — go deep in 1-2 areas

Stanford.overview: Stanford University — Silicon Valley's hub for innovation, entrepreneurship, and interdisciplinary thinking. ~3.6% acceptance rate.
what_matters: Recommendation letters from mentors who know you

Harvard.overview: Harvard University — the world's most prestigious university, known for liberal arts, research, and global leadership. ~3.2% acceptance rate.

Oxford.overview: University of Oxford — the oldest university in the English-speaking world, renowned for tutorial system and academic rigor. ~17% acceptance rate.
what_matters: Strong admissions test scores (MAT, PAT, etc.)

Cambridge.overview: University of Cambridge — historic center of scientific discovery and academic excellence. ~21% acceptance rate.

study_tips.spaced_repetition: Review material at increasing intervals: 1 day, 3 days, 1 week, 2 weeks. This builds long-term memory far better than cramming.
study_tips.active_recall: Test yourself instead of re-reading. Close the book and write what you remember. This strengthens neural pathways.
study_tips.pomodoro_technique: Work for 25 minutes, break for 5 minutes. After 4 cycles, take a 15-30 minute break. Maintains focus without burnout.
study_tips.elaborative_interrogation: Ask 'why?' and 'how?' about every concept. Connect new information to what you already know.
study_tips.interleaving: Mix different subjects in one study session instead of grinding one topic. It feels harder but improves retention.
